scope: 24 new nominated main book records across innovation, engineering, infrastructure, computing, energy, scaling, and space technology. All nominated eligible works are scored, including below-target works.

notes: Historical selection underweights public support; no near-perfect evidence mark.
Connects invention, experimentation, production, institutions and commercial adoption.
Incremental improvement and deployment constraints transfer well.

Case accumulation adds some repetition.

books.case: The useful material concerns the difference between an invention and its affordable, reliable deployment. Muldoon's strongly favourable review also acknowledges that government partnership is undervalued. The author's interview makes the minimal-government conclusion explicit. V5 is applied to the sustained political-economic advocacy, not to the author's affiliations. The counterfactual retains the useful innovation history.
books.objection: A preferred institutional model does too much explanatory work. Positive examples do not establish that public research and private development are substitutes.
books.eligibility: Narrative and argument pass the hard exclusions. V5 applies at a serious level to the governing advocacy. V1/V2 are not separately asserted from a disagreement about policy; V3/V4 do not apply.
books.theme: T11=0: neither a single-nation history nor predominantly an unwanted topic. T12=0: innovation remains the organising subject. The ideological conclusion triggers V5, but does not establish that politics predominates over technological development. H13=0: cross-period account with no single historical endpoint. P14 uses 2020, not the paperback year.

notes: Research-informed examples, but selection and classification of innovations remain weakly controlled.
Connects networks, institutions, technical knowledge and environments for discovery.
Useful for structuring research and preserving incomplete ideas.
Plausible mechanisms; less analysis of when openness creates costly errors.
Seven patterns provide a compact, organised argument.
Knowledge recombination and research networks remain useful subjects.

Skilled synthesis with serious critical engagement.
Strong cumulative structure and memorable examples.
Concepts such as good and successful ideas need sharper separation.
books.case: The best payload is how environments support recombination, slow development and exchange of ideas. Shalizi credits the attempt to compare a larger set of innovations, while questioning sampling, definitions and error trade-offs. These are score reductions, not proof that the central account has no value.
books.objection: A successful idea is not necessarily a good idea. Benefits of open exploration need to be weighed against the cost of false positives.
books.eligibility: A sustained explanatory account rather than a training procedure. No serious veto established. Political implications are auxiliary to the account of innovation.
books.theme: T11=T12=0: innovation is central; institutions and policy are applications. H13=0: cross-period comparative argument. P14 uses the original 2010 release.

notes: Observed building changes and practitioner evidence; illustrative cases are not controlled comparisons.
Links physical layers, maintenance, users, ownership, cost and institutional adaptation.
Exceptional reuse in modular systems, replacement cycles and designing for change.
Different rates of change explain important interface and maintenance failures.
Images and text supply substantial evidence in a compact volume.
Adaptation and maintenance remain durable constraints.
Infrastructure, engineering and reliability fit directly.
Long specialist engagement; author synthesises practitioner knowledge.
Visual sequences make change over time clear.
Concepts and physical examples are expressed precisely.
books.case: This is one of the strongest discoveries for reusable engineering thought. It treats buildings as systems that change after completion. Its comparative argument and visual evidence dominate; it is not a construction specification or procedural design manual. The publication and obscurity deductions nevertheless prevent it from reaching 92 even with perfect positive marks.
books.objection: Selected adaptable buildings cannot by themselves establish a universal design rule; some uses need greater initial constraint or integration.
books.eligibility: Passes hard exclusion 2 with moderate confidence: architectural criticism and a sustained account of adaptation dominate over incidental design advice. No serious veto established.
books.theme: T11=0: individual structures and adaptation, not urban history. T12=0: engineering and maintenance are central. H13=0: an argument about change across eras, not one historical period. P14 uses 1994, not the 1995 paperback.

notes: Concrete engineering explanations; historical priority claims warrant some caution.

Basic engineering principles age well.

books.case: Seven component families connect everyday mechanisms to larger technologies. This provides a good account of technical recombination. For a theoretical physicist, the limiting factor is not readability but the amount of unfamiliar strategic content beyond elementary mechanics.
books.objection: Breadth of applications does not equal deep integration of production, institutions and trade.
books.eligibility: Explanatory engineering history for general readers, not instructions for designing or operating equipment. No serious veto established.
books.theme: T11=T12=0. Personal and medical examples are auxiliary to component engineering. H13=0: a cross-period account of inventions and current applications. P14 uses 2023.

A readable tour organised around physical problems.

books.case: The book explains structures through engineering problems, materials and failure cases, with practitioner experience. It passes as narrative explanation. Its main limitation for this profile is the introductory level and limited integration with industrial organisation and trade.
books.objection: A broad introduction to structures cannot supply exceptional strategic novelty to an advanced physics reader.
books.eligibility: General-reader explanatory narrative; no course exercises, design specification system or operating procedure governs the book. No serious veto established.
books.theme: T11=0: building engineering is not urban history. T12=0. H13=0: ancient and modern structures serve a cross-period explanation. P14 uses 2018; the 2019 paperback does not reset it.

notes: Extensive reporting and access; treatment of industry actors requires critical distance.

books.case: A substantial energy-system synthesis spanning fuel supply, electricity, technology and security. It is closer to the desired profile than a book centred only on oil diplomacy. Its scale, age and reader-count deduction make it a poor candidate for the specific >92 search.
books.objection: Industry access is not independent confirmation; the long narrative sometimes gives prominent actors more room than causal analysis.
books.eligibility: Narrative synthesis, not a technical manual. No serious veto established. Read its outlook as a dated outlook, not a statement of 2026 conditions.
books.theme: T11=T12=0: energy provision is the organising subject; climate, finance and politics are interacting domains. H13=0: historical reconstruction and forward-looking system analysis lack one central bounded period. P14 uses 2011, not the updated paperback.

notes: Substantial reporting; attribution across a long computing history is not uniformly secure.

Useful lessons about complementary skills and invention becoming usable systems.
Collaboration is explained better than detailed technical or comparative causal mechanisms.

books.case: A connected history of the people and teams behind computing. The transferable value lies in complementary skills and the relation between invention and implementation. Narrative range earns a high integration score, but it is not sufficient evidence for top marks in mechanism or factual completeness.
books.objection: Memorable collaboration stories are not a controlled explanation of why some research and product teams succeed while others fail.
books.eligibility: Narrative computing history passes both hard exclusions. No serious veto established by the inspected evidence. Minor or local historical weaknesses are retained in E, not converted into an unsupported central-failure veto.
books.theme: T11=0: the technical developments have global influence, even where many cases are American. T12=0. H13=0: the comparative account spans several eras from early computing concepts to networked computing without one bounded central period. P14 uses 2014.

books.format: hardcover; no verified English paperback identified

books.case: A readable account of how the commercial Internet developed, centred on the browser era through the first iPhone. It connects product decisions and business models. This is useful context for platform transitions, but the evidence does not justify exceptional scores in mechanism and generality.
books.objection: Prominent winning companies dominate the story; hindsight can make contingent outcomes appear inevitable.
books.eligibility: Narrative history, not a computing course or operating guide. No serious veto established.
books.theme: T11=0: largely American companies, but global technological influence. T12=0: computing platforms are central, finance and media business are applications. H13 uses 2007, the iPhone endpoint identified by the review; endpoint confidence high. P14 uses 2018.

books.objection: Facility visits reveal the system's physical shape but provide less quantitative depth on its performance and economics.
books.eligibility: Narrative nonfiction, no instructional or reference purpose. No serious veto established.
books.theme: T11=T12=0: physical computing infrastructure is central. H13=0: a contemporary reported system account, not a book about a bounded historic period; publication age is handled only by P14. Original year 2012.

notes: Extensive quantitative synthesis; limits and substitutions remain contested in its wider conclusions.
Unusually broad integration of biological, physical, industrial and social systems.

books.case: This broad synthesis is relevant to quantification and scaling. It is not hard-excluded merely for equations or difficulty: the subject crosses disciplines and its purpose is explanation rather than specialist training. Some critics challenge its treatment of substitution and the implications of physical limits; that disagreement limits E and M without proving a central factual failure.
books.objection: A fitted growth pattern is not automatically an explanation. The book's large reading cost also makes a near-perfect density score unjustified.
books.eligibility: Passes hard exclusion 2 with moderate confidence as a cross-disciplinary explanatory synthesis, not a narrow technical monograph. Environmental implications do not dominate the whole work as an activist programme. No serious veto established.
books.theme: T11=0: biology, cities and environmental limits are parts of a broader growth study, not predominant excluded themes. T12=0. H13=0: comparative growth across scales and eras. P14 uses 2019, not the 2020 paperback.

books.objection: Breadth and numerical detail are not sufficient for full systems-integration or strategic-utility marks.
books.eligibility: General explanatory nonfiction, not a course or specialist reference. No serious veto established.
books.theme: T11=T12=0: size and technical scaling are central. H13=0: no central historical period. P14 uses 2023.

notes: Strong research into constraints; weaker legal interpretations and conflict arguments prevent a higher mark.

books.case: The strongest new candidate in this search is a systems audit of space settlement. It goes beyond rockets to the requirements for keeping a population alive and supplied. The technical dependency analysis has broad use for project assessment. Foust, however, identifies weaker policy material and disputed interpretations of the Artemis Accords and astronaut-rescue obligations. These prevent an evidence score high enough to clear 92.
books.objection: Sound engineering objections do not by themselves establish the book's broader claims about conflict or the optimal timing of settlement. Hague supplies an opposing view, but his own extrapolations are not treated as proof that those engineering constraints vanish.
books.eligibility: Sustained explanatory argument, not a settlement procedure. No serious veto established: the principal technical case survives the identified weaker sections. The book is assessed as project feasibility, not as an ideological anti-space manifesto; this classification has moderate confidence.
books.theme: T11=0: physiology and environmental conditions are settlement requirements, not a disease or ecological history. T12=0: law and conflict are auxiliary constraints within the central technology-and-settlement question. H13=0: no historical period. P14 uses 2023, not the 2025 paperback.

notes: Expert interviews and explicit obstacles support the account; emerging fields retain uncertainty.
Connects technical feasibility and economics, but largely in separate technology chapters.

books.case: A survey of emerging technologies that pays attention to obstacles and economics. It avoids an automatic hype veto because uncertainty and failure are part of its purpose. Chris Lee found the treatment accurate but too shallow for readers seeking depth, which matters strongly for this profile.
books.objection: Short surveys of ten technologies cannot each provide the mechanism and strategic depth required for an exceptional score.
books.eligibility: Narrative popular science, not a technical manual. V4 is not established: the book critically examines prospective technologies rather than depending primarily on unqualified revolutionary promises.
books.theme: T11=T12=0: no unwanted theme predominates over the technology survey. H13=0. P14 uses 2017, not the 2019 paperback. The observed count is below 1,000, so O15 applies.

notes: Research-based economic account; technological demonstrations cannot settle aggregate outcomes.
Connects digital capabilities, complements, productivity, skills and distribution.
Useful for thinking about adoption and complementary investment.

books.case: A useful account of digital technology and economic complements, with implications for productivity and labour. The strongest material distinguishes technical capability from how gains are distributed. Its forecasts and aggregate inferences are too uncertain for near-perfect evidence or durability marks.
books.objection: A convincing demonstration of a technology does not establish the timing, scale or distribution of its economy-wide effects.
books.eligibility: General explanatory economics, not specialist training. No serious veto established: policy recommendations are secondary to the analytical account, and its value does not rest solely on a prediction.
books.theme: T11=T12=0: computing-driven production and productivity are central; economic policy is an application. H13=0: contemporary argument, not a bounded historical account. P14 uses 2014.

books.format: hardcover; no verified English paperback identified

books.case: The maintenance argument is highly relevant, but the book also advances a sustained manifesto about American work and its institutions. The publisher explicitly identifies this purpose, and the excerpt develops it. Under the user's V5, the useful technical-organisational payload does not remove the veto.
books.objection: Maintenance and innovation often reinforce each other. Treating their advocates as opposing camps can obscure that relationship.
books.eligibility: Passes hard exclusions as a sustained argument. V5 applies to its manifesto and civil-economic advocacy. No independent V1/V2 finding is made; the counterfactual preserves the strong maintenance content.
books.theme: T11=-10: the governing diagnosis and reform target concern American work and public infrastructure. T12=0: maintenance and reliability remain the main operational subject; advocacy triggers V5 without automatically making politics the predominant topic. H13=0: contemporary and cross-period argument. P14 uses 2020.

notes: Relevant engineering knowledge and reporting; policy prescriptions require separate justification.

Personal and normative passages reduce technical density.

Readable movement from systems to their implications.

books.case: The engineering explanation is strong. The book also makes collective transformation toward equitable and sustainable infrastructure a sustained purpose, not a brief application. The publisher's account and Lam's review support that classification. V5 therefore applies under this repository's broad activism rule, while the counterfactual credits the technical substance.
books.objection: Describing an engineering constraint does not uniquely determine a social programme for meeting it.
books.eligibility: Narrative explanatory nonfiction passes hard exclusions. V5 applies to the sustained environmental and civic transformation programme; moderate confidence because engineering explanation occupies much of the book. No claim of factual unreliability is implied by this veto.
books.theme: T11=T12=0: infrastructure is the central subject, and the evidence does not establish that environmental topics or politics predominate over it. V5 and thematic predominance are separate tests. H13=0. P14 uses 2023, not the 2025 paperback.

reviews: Howard Chudacoff, American Journal of Play
notes: Documented histories, with overly linear causal chains and loose definitions.
Connects leisure, materials, mechanisms, commerce and technical spillovers.
Useful reminder to inspect unexpected application domains, not a predictive method.
Some causal links are suggestive rather than established.
Engaging cases carry moderate narrative overhead.
Historical spillover mechanisms remain useful.
Innovation fits; leisure and cultural history reduce directness.
Experienced synthesist with specialist historical review.
Strong storytelling and clear chapter structure.
Play, pleasure and novelty are not always distinguished precisely.
books.case: A history of technical spillovers from amusement and consumer desire. Chudacoff praises its examples but questions linear chains of historical causation and the loose definition of play. This leaves useful material without supporting a near-perfect mechanistic score.
books.objection: Tracing a chain from a plaything to a later technology does not establish that play was the decisive cause.
books.eligibility: Nonfiction explanatory history, distinct from similarly titled novels and stage works. No serious veto established.
books.theme: T11=T12=0: technological spillovers from leisure are central, not sport or media politics. H13=0: broad cross-period account. P14 uses 2016.

notes: Well-reported analogy, but technological determinism limits inference.
Links infrastructure economics, electrification, computing and institutional effects.
Useful distinction between shared infrastructure and differentiated applications.
Explains utility economics better than all downstream social consequences.
Compact argument; social speculation is less efficient.
Cloud-infrastructure economics lasts better than contemporary forecasts.
Computing and infrastructure fit directly.
Experienced technology journalist; limited independent causal testing.
Clear analogy and readable exposition.
Some broad claims need more qualification.
books.case: The utility-computing analogy remains useful for thinking about scale and where differentiation moves when infrastructure becomes shared. Horn challenges the tendency to equate common infrastructure with absence of competitive advantage. This is a good strategic question, not an exceptional complete model.
books.objection: Electricity and computing are not identical: common computing resources can still support highly differentiated software and organisational capabilities.
books.eligibility: Explanatory argument, not a cloud-computing manual. No serious veto established; the durable infrastructure argument remains independently useful despite dated predictions.
books.theme: T11=T12=0: technical infrastructure and its economics organise the account. H13=0: a cross-period analogy, not one bounded history. P14 uses 2008, not the later paperback.

notes: Firsthand scientific history, with memoir selection and perspective limits.
Chemistry, testing, handling, procurement and performance interact; wider economy is less developed.
Excellent lessons about optimisation under competing practical constraints.
Failure modes and trade-offs have unusually concrete physical explanations.
Compact technical history with substantial information per episode.
Experimental discipline and physical trade-offs remain durable.
Engineering, high-tech development and reliability fit directly.
Author was a direct participant in propellant research.
Memorable narrative makes difficult material manageable.
Humour is effective but occasionally displaces exact qualification.
books.case: A technical memoir and history of the search for usable rocket propellants. Its main purpose is to explain how research unfolded, not to train the reader to formulate fuels or operate propulsion hardware. The payload is engineering trade-offs: performance must coexist with handling, storage, reliability and cost.
books.objection: The coverage is narrower than the best cross-industry systems books, and the original historical account is old despite its recent reissue.
books.eligibility: Passes hard exclusion 2 with moderate confidence: narrative scientific history dominates the technical material. V3's science-memoir exception is consistent with, but not needed to override, that prior decision. No serious veto established.
books.theme: T11=0: the technology has international influence and the account includes international work. T12=0: propellant engineering is central; military procurement is an application. H13 uses approximately 1970, the end of the participant research period described by the scope review; endpoint confidence moderate. P14 uses 1972, not 2018.

reviews: Kirkus critical review and original year
notes: Historically grounded design cases; a dominant explanatory lens still needs limits.
Links user needs, material form, manufacturing, competition and improvement.
Strong reusable habit of analysing shortcomings and practical trade-offs.
Shows how constraints shape successive designs.
Repeated examples substantially lower length efficiency.
Design constraints and imperfect optimisation remain durable.
Invention and engineering improvement fit directly.
Established engineering scholar and historian.
Readable cases, with repetition limiting progression.

books.case: An explanatory history of ordinary artefacts, organised around how dissatisfaction and constraints drive redesign. The argument is transferable beyond small objects. Kirkus identifies persistent repetition, so density cannot receive the near-perfect mark needed for 92.
books.objection: The same improvement principle appears in too many cases; an explanatory heuristic is not a complete theory of invention.
books.eligibility: Sustained narrative and explanatory argument, not a product-design instruction manual. No serious veto established.
books.theme: T11=T12=0. H13=0: a cross-period account of artefact evolution without one central historical interval. P14 uses 1992; the 1994 paperback date is not the original year.

excluded.title: Loonshots
excluded.author: Safi Bahcall
excluded.reason: The governing purpose is to teach leaders how to organise and nurture breakthrough projects. Historical cases and the phase-transition analogy support an actionable management framework and its rules. Under the strict rule excluding works primarily structured to develop an applied skill, this is an instructional management book. Its substantial history makes the boundary judgment moderate rather than high confidence; accessible narrative and a physicist author do not override the instructional purpose. No score is assigned.

excluded.title: Creativity, Inc.
excluded.author: Ed Catmull; Amy Wallace
excluded.reason: The memoir supports a book primarily organised to teach creative management: protecting new work, handling failure, communication practices, and sustaining a creative organisation. The publisher description, opening management example and contents establish that practical training purpose. The science-biography exception cannot override hard exclusion 2. The 2023 expansion does not change this classification. No score is assigned.

excluded.title: Engineering in Plain Sight
excluded.author: Grady Hillhouse
excluded.reason: An illustrated field guide arranged for identification and lookup of infrastructure components. Its detailed contents are separate reference entries for structures and equipment, rather than a sustained narrative or argument. It serves non-engineers, which does not by itself exempt a predominantly technical-reference structure under the rule's positive narrative/explanation requirement. No score is assigned.

excluded.title: How Technology Works
excluded.author: DK
excluded.reason: A visual reference organised as individual devices grouped for easy lookup, with stepwise technical explanations. It is introductory, but its primary structure is reference rather than a sustained narrative or explanatory argument across the system. This applies the rule's required structure test, not a claim that the book is written only for experts. No score is assigned.
